scenario: A 'family safety' location app is present with monitoring capability broader than typical parental-control disclosure.

supported_findings: The app requests ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION, READ_SMS, and includes a 60-second location-ping-interval string, indicating frequent background location reporting plus SMS content logging.
A string named stealth_mode_enabled indicates the app has a mode designed to reduce its visibility to the device user, which is broader than disclosure typical of consented parental-control tools.
The app is digitally signed by an identifiable, non-self-signed publisher (FamilySafety Corp), unlike the anonymized certificates in most other cases in this set.
unsupported_claims_to_watch_for: Any claim identifying who installed this app, who is being monitored, or the relationship between them (e.g. 'a parent monitoring a child' or 'a partner monitoring a partner') -- no such identity evidence exists in this case.
Any claim that SMS content or location history was actually reviewed by any person.
Any claim that stealth_mode_enabled was active at any specific time -- only the string's presence is observed.
